text:
incident-bot: [P2] GPU_ECC_Error_Rate spike detected in west-1 pool — 9 events in 10m across multiple nodes, auto-pages oncall
Jordan: spotted short ECC bursts + a couple of kernel recoveries on a subset of A100s. not catastrophic but causing node churn if drains kick.
Kai: can reproduce via telemetry, looks like correlated with a scheduled batch migration that started ~2159k. sequence lengths jumped. link: https://prom.redwood/gpu/queries?range=15m&query=gpu_ecc_errors_total%5B5m%5D%20by%20(node)
Lina: customer impact check: three heavy-batch tenants saw elevated retry rates, one reported increased 429s from batch controller. opened CS tickets and flagged to AE.
Jordan: short plan: 1) reduce pager noise 2) pause auto-drain for affected nodes 3) mitigate load from noisy batch jobs (throttle/reroute) 4) create quick panel for VRAM/kernels/ECC to monitor live.
Priya: adding a 20m silence for GPU_ECC alerts in west-1 while we investigate: `amtool silence add "gpu-ecc-west1-temp" -n 20m --match 'alertname=GPU_ECC_Errors,region=west-1'`
ops-bot: Silence added by Priya — id=sl-2026-342, expires in 20m.
Kai: I'm going to scale down the nightly batch job replica count for the two offending namespaces and add a temporary rate limit on sequence length via feature-flag. Patching job controllers now.
Jordan: to avoid oscillating drains, I'm toggling the node annotation that blocks automatic cordon/drain: `kubectl annotate node node-7redwood drain-protection=enabled --overwrite` (we'll remove after triage).
Lina: good call. customer note draft: "We observed transient ECC memory error spikes affecting a subset of GPU nodes during nightly batch migration which led to increased retries for some heavy workloads. We applied mitigations and are monitoring. No user requests failed."
Kai: created a minimal dashboard: `/dashboards/gpu/triage/ecc-vram-live` with these panels: ECC error rate by node, VRAM used per pod (top 15), kernel_recovers. link (internal): https://dash.redwood/gpu/triage/ecc-vram-live
Priya: suggested interim alert adjustments: increase ECC rate threshold for west-1 to 8 events/10m and add an annotation to suppress during scheduled migrations. pushing a draft alert change: https://git.redwood/ops/alerts/merge_requests/623
Jordan: sample PromQLs for the panel and postmortem notes: `sum by(node) (increase(gpu_ecc_errors_total[10m]))`, `max_over_time(gpu_vram_used_bytes[5m])`, `count_over_time(gpu_kernel_recoveries_total[10m])`
Kai: ran memtest-lite on the 3 highest-hit nodes, one node showed repeated ECC counts after memtest -> captured dmesg and NVML logs, collected via `gpu-log-collector --since 1h --nodes node-3,node-7,node-12` and uploaded to artifacts.
Lina: CS update: AE notified two customers, scheduled callback tomorrow 09:30 PT. raised transparency flag in CS playbook.
Priya: I'm going to create two follow-up tickets: (A) fleet firmware audit for west-1, (B) alert redesign to include suppression windows tied to batch schedules.
Jordan: I'll own the firmware audit ticket and coordinate with hw-ops. Kai will own telemetry/dashboard improvements. Lina please keep CS comms.
Priya: tickets created: https://git.redwood/ops/issues/5720 (firmware-audit-west1), https://git.redwood/ops/issues/5721 (alerts-suppression-for-batches), https://git.redwood/telemetry/issues/1102 (per-model seq-length surfacing)
ops-bot: Created dashboard shortlink and attached to ticket ops/5721.
Kai: handoff: I'm taking monitoring ownership for next 4 hours — watch for ECC counts after silence expiration at 2162346790, verify `increase(gpu_ecc_errors_total[10m]) < 8` for 1h before reverting thresholds, escalate if node drain re-triggers.
Jordan: note — if ECC returns with kernel oops escalate to oncall SE and prepare for rolling maintenance window.
incident-bot: Incident state -> MONITORED. Reason: temporary noise due to batch migration; mitigations applied (silence, throttle, node protection, dashboard). Follow-ups filed.
Lina: reminder: schedule a 30min post-incident sync next Wed to decide long-term alert thresholds, if we need suppression tied to job schedules, and whether to pursue firmware/driver roll.
Priya: will rollback temp thresholds 24h after no recurrence, or sooner if noise resumes. :thumbsup:
Kai: leaving final note: added runbook snippet to ops playbook: 
```
# ECC burst triage (summary)
1. Silence alerts briefly to stop pager churn
2. Throttle noisy batch jobs / reduce replicas
3. Block auto-drain with node annotation
4. Run memtest & collect NVML / dmesg logs
5. If recurring, schedule maintenance and replace hardware
```
Jordan: thanks team — quick, calm handling. monitoring until handoff complete.
